[Source 1] Quantization for LLMs: GPTQ, QLoRA, and INT8 Inference Techniques
d mixed CPU/GPU inference, enabling quantized LLaMA models to run on Apple Silicon, consumer gaming GPUs, and CPUs. Supported quantization types include Q4_K_M (4-bit with mixed 6-bit precision for critical layers), providing the best quality-size trade-off. llama.cpp achieves 30-50 tokens/second on Apple M2 Pro for Llama 3 8B in Q4_K_M quantization. AWQ (Activation-aware Weight Quantization, Lin et al., 2023) identifies salient weight channels corresponding to large-magnitude activations and applies higher precision only to those channels, achieving 4-bit quality closer to FP16 than GPTQ. LLM.int8() (Dettmers et al., 2022) handles outlier activations via mixed-precision decomposition, enabling 8-bit inference with negligible quality loss for models up to 175B parameters.

ained on 15 trillion tokens with a 128K vocabulary tokenizer, achieving 82.0% on MMLU and setting new open-source performance standards across reasoning, coding, and multilingual tasks.

[Source 3] LLM Evaluation Frameworks: HELM, BIG-Bench, and MMLU Benchmarks
tect. Dynamic benchmarks such as LiveBench (White et al., 2024) use freshly generated questions (math competitions, coding contests post-training-cutoff) to prevent contamination. MT-Bench (Zheng et al., 2023) uses GPT-4 as a judge to score multi-turn conversation quality across writing, roleplay, extraction, reasoning, math, coding, and STEM domains (scores 1-10). LLM-as-judge approaches show high correlation with human preferences (Spearman ρ≈0.9) but suffer from position bias (favoring first responses) and verbosity bias. Arena-style evaluation (Chatbot Arena, LMSYS) uses Elo ratings from millions of blind pairwise human preference votes, providing contamination-resistant evaluation at scale, with GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, and Gemini 1.5 Pro consistently at the top.
